courses.name: Principles of Imperative Computation
courses.description: Develops imperative programs from algorithms, emphasizing correctness, foundational data structures and C programming.
courses.prerequisites: 15-112 Min. grade C or 02-120 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: Imperative programming, correctness methods and implementation of basic data structures/algorithms establish computing foundations.

courses.name: Principles of Functional Programming
courses.description: Studies functional programming through functions, types, recursion, induction and modular program design.
courses.prerequisites: ( 21-127 Min. grade C or 15-151 Min. grade C or 21-128 Min. grade C) and 15-112 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: Functional programming, types, recursion and modular program construction establish computing foundations.

courses.name: Parallel and Sequential Data Structures and Algorithms
courses.description: Covers design, analysis and implementation of parallel and sequential algorithms and data structures, with practical programming applications.
courses.prerequisites: 15-150 Min. grade C and 15-122 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: Design, analysis and implementation of sequential/parallel data structures and algorithms establish computing foundations.

courses.name: Introduction to Computer Systems
courses.description: Explains program execution, memory and communication from a programmer’s perspective, with attention to performance, portability and robustness.
courses.prerequisites: 15-122 Min. grade C

category_review.rationale: The programmer-facing study of program execution, storage and communication, preparing for architecture/operating systems/networks, establishes computing systems rather than general programming.

courses.name: Great Ideas in Theoretical Computer Science
courses.description: Applies mathematical reasoning and proof to computational problems, drawing on algorithms, complexity, probability, graphs and related theory.
courses.prerequisites: ( 15-122 Min. grade C or 15-150 Min. grade C) and ( 15-151 Min. grade C or 21-128 Min. grade C or 21-127 Min. grade C)

category_review.rationale: Theoretical computer-science problem solving spans algorithms, complexity, automata and computation. Mathematics supports those foundational computing methods.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning I
courses.description: Introduces search, probability, machine learning and reinforcement learning through theory and implementations of influential AI systems; includes responsible AI development.
courses.prerequisites: ( 15-122 Min. grade C or 15-121 Min. grade C) and ( 21-241 Min. grade C or 18-202 Min. grade C or 21-240 Min. grade C or 21-254 Min. grade C) and ( 21-128 Min. grade C or 21-127 Min. grade C or 15-151 Min. grade C)

category_review.rationale: Search, machine learning, reinforcement learning and implementation of intelligent systems establish AI/ML methods.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning II
courses.description: Extends the introductory AI/ML sequence with deeper foundations and recent advances, building on 07-280.
courses.prerequisites: 07-280 Min. grade C and 21-122 Min. grade C and ( 36-218 Min. grade C or 21-325 Min. grade C or 15-259 Min. grade C or 36-225 Min. grade C or 36-235 Min. grade C)

category_review.rationale: The second AI/ML course extends core methods and current AI research; its primary subject is AI/ML.

courses.name: Natural Language Processing
courses.description: Covers computational representations of language, language models and machine-learning methods for NLP tasks such as translation, information extraction and question answering. Programming assignments and a project emphasize rapid prototyping.

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.description: Introduces image processing, detection and recognition, geometric and physical models of vision, sensing and video analysis, with practical work on visual-computing problems. The catalog limits enrollment to undergraduates.

courses.description: Develops mathematical proof through logic, sets, induction, functions and combinatorics. The directory limits enrollment to incoming CS freshmen; it does not define whether this label includes BSAI. A grade of C or better is needed for later CS prerequisites.

courses.name: Concepts of Mathematics
courses.description: Develops mathematical reasoning and proof through logic, sets, functions, number theory and real numbers.
courses.prerequisites: 15-112 Min. grade C or 02-120 Min. grade C or 21-108 Min. grade C or 21-090 Min. grade A or 21-120 Min. grade C or 21-112 Min. grade C

courses.name: Differential and Integral Calculus
courses.description: Introduces single-variable differentiation and integration, with approximation and optimization applications.

courses.name: Integration and Approximation
courses.description: Develops integration methods and approximation, including numerical methods, differential equations, sequences and series.

courses.name: Matrices and Linear Transformations
courses.description: Introduces linear algebra, including matrix systems, vector spaces, linear transformations, orthogonality, eigenvalues and elementary proofs. The catalog strongly recommends 21-127; it does not list a formal prerequisite field.

courses.name: Calculus in Three Dimensions
courses.description: Studies multivariable derivatives, integrals and vector calculus in three dimensions.

courses.name: Vector Calculus using Matrix Algebra
courses.description: Uses matrix algebra in multivariable calculus. Intended especially for SCS students but open across colleges; treated as equivalent to 21-259 for prerequisite purposes.
courses.prerequisites: 21-122 and ( 21-241 Min. grade B or 21-242 Min. grade B)

courses.name: Multidimensional Calculus
courses.description: Develops multidimensional calculus with a stronger emphasis on mathematical reasoning and proof.

courses.name: Vector Analysis
courses.description: Provides an honors treatment of vector analysis with substantial proof work.
courses.prerequisites: 21-122 and ( 15-151 or 21-127 ) and ( 21-242 Min. grade B or 21-241 Min. grade A)

courses.name: Probability Theory for Computer Scientists
courses.description: Introduces probability and random processes through computer-science applications. Progression to 36-226/326/410 requires C or better; Statistics majors/minors must take 36-226, while other students earning B or better may proceed directly to 36-401.

courses.name: Probability and Computing
courses.description: Introduces probability for computing, motivated by machine learning, randomized algorithms, systems performance and current research.
courses.prerequisites: ( 16-211 Min. grade C or 21-259 Min. grade C or 21-266 Min. grade C or 21-268 Min. grade C) and ( 15-151 Min. grade B or 21-127 Min. grade B or 21-128 Min. grade B or 15-251 Min. grade C)

courses.name: Probability
courses.description: Studies probability models, random variables, conditioning, limit theorems and applications. The prose recommends 21-127 rather than requiring it individually; the formal prerequisite field permits it as one alternative.

courses.name: Introduction to Statistical Inference
courses.description: Studies estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, regression and variance analysis. Progression to 36-401, 36-402 or a 36-46x course requires C or better.
courses.prerequisites: 21-325 Min. grade C or 15-259 Min. grade C or 36-218 Min. grade C or 36-217 Min. grade C or 36-219 Min. grade C or 36-225 Min. grade C or 21-425 Min. grade C

courses.name: Probability and Martingales
courses.description: Develops probability and martingale theory in an honors course.
courses.prerequisites: ( 21-127 Min. grade A or 21-128 Min. grade A or 15-151 Min. grade A) and ( 21-268 Min. grade B or 21-266 Min. grade A or 21-259 Min. grade A or 21-269 Min. grade B)

courses.name: Introduction to Probability Theory
courses.description: Introduces probability distributions, independence, conditional probability and limit theorems. Enrollment requires sophomore standing or higher.

courses.name: Probability and Statistical Inference I
courses.description: Begins an integrated probability and inference sequence using distributions, estimation, tests and regression. Limited to Statistics majors/minors and sophomore standing or higher; consult Statistics advisers for the declaration deadline. Prior credit in 36-217/218/219/700, 21-325 or 15-259 excludes enrollment. C or better is needed to progress to 36-236/226 or 36-410.

courses.name: Probability and Statistical Inference II
courses.description: Continues probability and inference through discrete and multivariate distributions with estimation, testing and regression. Limited to Statistics majors/minors or CS majors taking both 36-235 and 36-236; others are directed to 36-226. The source does not explain whether its CS-major exception includes BSAI. C or better is needed to progress to 36-401.
courses.prerequisites: 36-235 Min. grade C

courses.name: Modern Regression
courses.description: Applies regression and model checking to real data, emphasizing defensible conclusions and scientific reporting. Progression to 36-402 or a 36-46x course requires C; the prose identifies the spring section as primarily for SCS students.

requirements.title: Conditional admission and transfer rules
requirements.summary: SCS entrants declare a major in first-year spring. Internal SCS transfers depend on interest, ability and space after consultation; no grade cutoff is specified. Transfers from other CMU schools or dual-degree applicants must complete 15-122, 15-150, 07-280, 07-380, one of 15-210/15-213/15-251, and one of 15-259/21-325/21-425/36-218/36-225; expected QPA across these six is at least 3.6 and overall QPA at least 3.0. Starting Fall 2026, apply to a specific major only once. Deadlines are last classes of mini-1, mini-3 or mini-6; review includes coursework, computing involvement and an essay. External university transfers apply through Admissions; admission depends on space and preparation. Admitted external transfers must remain in their initial SCS major at least one year and meet the internal transfer criteria before changing, excluding transferred courses.

requirements.title: Graduation and residence
requirements.summary: Complete the degree program with cumulative CMU QPA at least 2.00, SCS faculty recommendation, and fulfilled university financial obligations. Residence requires at least four full-time semesters or equivalent part-time study at CMU, comprising at least 180 units.

requirements.title: Good academic standing
requirements.summary: Maintain semester and cumulative QPA at least 2.00. Complete attempted foundational courses by the end of sophomore year, in at most two attempts each: C or better in 15-112, 15-122 and 15-151 (or 21-127), and D or better in 21-120 and 21-122.

requirements.title: AI-specific academic progress
requirements.summary: Complete 07-280 and the required probability course with C or better by the end of sophomore year. Complete at least one of 15-210, 15-213 or 15-251 with D or better by the end of junior year. Major-specific progress courses allow at most two attempts each. Academic-action procedures apply when good-standing conditions are unmet.

requirements.title: Current science approval rules
requirements.summary: Current science rules supplement the catalog: consult an SCS adviser before registration for every selected course; minis need adviser/associate-dean review. ECE graduate courses (18-6xx through 18-9xx) are excluded. Unlisted Engineering & Public Policy courses require adviser/associate-dean suitability review. SCS crosslists or substantial mathematical/computational content generally disqualify a course.

requirements.title: Current humanities approval rules
requirements.summary: Current humanities rules permit two minis totaling at least nine units to fulfill one breadth category only with associate-dean permission and suitable category goals. Lower-unit humanities/arts courses may combine into one nine-unit elective with adviser and associate-dean approval. AI uses Category 1A; other Category 1 options are excluded from this AI inventory.

requirements.title: Grading and repeated credit
requirements.summary: Pass/no-pass may be elected for a free elective unless disallowed; A–D earns P credit without QPA points. Audit earns no credit. Repeated-course grades all affect QPA, but units count once; repeating a passed course needs dean/department-head approval. Course prerequisites and corequisites must be met.

requirements.title: Transfer and examination credit
requirements.summary: Transfer credit needs official final transcripts, departmental equivalency/application review, and C− or better (including pass marks certified equivalent). No transfer math below Calculus I, English-language courses, career-preparation/first-year seminars or algebra-based physics. AP/IB credit applies only with home-unit approval; IB credit is restricted to Higher Level exams. Approved non-equivalent courses may count as electives or breadth where appropriate.

requirements.title: University graduation QPA exception
requirements.summary: University graduation rules allow a post-first-year QPA of at least 2.0 when a first-year entrant’s first-year grades alone cause cumulative QPA below 2.0. The transcript retains all grades; additional program QPA rules may apply, so SCS adviser confirmation is needed.

requirements.title: Certification, catalog and time limits
requirements.summary: Use applicable matriculation-catalog requirements and any approved College Council modifications. Standard study is eight semesters; earlier or longer completion is certified on meeting primary-degree requirements with adviser consultation. All degree units must be earned within eight years of award unless the dean grants a course-specific, time-bounded waiver based on currency, preparation and legitimate delay.

requirements.title: University residence and diploma conditions
requirements.summary: At least four full-time semesters or part-time equivalent and 180 units must be completed at CMU; exceptions require the home dean. Residence/course requirements, applicable QPA and financial obligations must be satisfied. These overlap the SCS graduation policy rather than adding units.

requirements.title: Optional honors thesis application
requirements.summary: Optional program: an SCS faculty adviser endorses a three-to-four-page prospectus describing the problem, significance, research plan/timeline and bibliography, with short abstract and adviser signature/email. Submit by senior-year start; junior-year submission is encouraged. There is no fixed QPA admission cutoff; 3.5 in relevant core topics is an expectation for success.

requirements.title: Optional honors thesis deliverables
requirements.summary: Normally 36 units over senior year (18 each semester), with a prior-work/progress paper, December poster, year-end poster and oral presentation, and written thesis. Optional 07-300 (9 units) and 07-400 practicum (12 units) prepare for research; practicum units may count toward the 36 thesis units when beginning that thesis. The major limits how thesis units fill electives.

requirements.title: Degree unit minimum
requirements.summary: The published degree summary requires 360 total units. Distribution totals are components of this total, not additional units.

requirements.title: Conditional eligibility for the Statistics sequence
requirements.summary: The 36-235/236 option is subject to course eligibility, not unrestricted BSAI enrollment: 36-235 requires Statistics major/minor status, sophomore standing and no prior credit in 36-217/218/219/700, 21-325 or 15-259. Consult Statistics advisers for the declaration deadline. 36-236 requires 36-235 with C or better and allows Statistics majors/minors or CS majors taking both courses; whether its CS-major exception includes BSAI is not defined. A declared Statistics-minor route is available under the university’s general minor-access rule; the minor separately requires at least three Statistics courses not counted toward the primary major. This optional minor adds its own requirements and is not required by the AI degree.

Source hierarchy is explicit: the general-education catalog describes its finite tables as approved in July 2026 and links separate up-to-date lists. Those current official lists govern the reconciled pools here. Exact current JSON feed URLs and inspection dates are registered. Catalog/current differences are documented in adapter NOTES; old removed options are not silently retained.

Science/humanities general-education nodes expand the primary degree totals and do not add a second set of units. Category 1A replaces Category 1 for AI. Optional thesis and transfer conditions are note branches; excluded courses are named in policy notes, not shown as approved options.

School and university QPA policies are both represented, including the university first-year exception and any additional program rules. Advisers determine individual applicability; completeness here concerns the published inventory rather than certification of a particular student.

Core course resources verified 2026-10-10: 07-280 and 07-380 identify Fall 2026. The linked 11-411 site and HTML syllabus are Spring 2026 examples; the 16-385 site contains a Spring 2020 syllabus. These historical resources do not replace 2026–2027 catalog requirements.

07-380 prerequisite discrepancy: the Fall 2026 course site lists 07-280 and a broader probability choice list, without the catalog’s 21-122 condition. The stored prerequisite expression remains the catalog version; confirm current registration eligibility with the department.

NLP and vision descriptions are paraphrased from their 2026–2027 SCS course-directory blocks. Course credits/prerequisites retain that source; public site and example syllabus provenance has separate term-specific source records.

2026-10-11: First-offered evidence now uses the current official catalog retrospective statement that BSAI started in Fall 2018. The older May 2018 announcement described the planned start and is retained as historical context.

2026-10-11: The Statistics-minor route establishes a conditional way to meet 36-235/236 eligibility; this does not infer that the undefined CS-major exception admits every AI-only student. University minor access and the Statistics minor double-count restriction have distinct sources. Adviser confirmation remains appropriate for AI-only enrollment and for the 15-151 CS-freshman label.

2026-10-11: Added Fall 2026 public resources for 15-122 and 15-210, plus an undated official-catalog-linked 15-251 instructional site. Only 15-122 is promoted as a public syllabus. The 15-210 home page says its syllabus is kept on Ed; the independently public policies page is not substituted as that syllabus.

2026-10-11: 15-122 Fall 2026 site describes AP/equivalent/adviser entry paths and recommends concurrent/prior mathematics. The stored prerequisites retain the formal current catalog expression; site-specific entry guidance is not silently merged into catalog rules.

2026-10-11: Existing program statements describe expected graduation learning, not measured attainment. Course learning-objective or grading pages do not establish program-assessed outcomes; no public program assessment results were verified in this bounded source set.

2026-10-11: The current directory links a Fall 2023 15-151/21-128 site and public syllabus; these are historical examples, not current prerequisites. The 15-259/559 site identifies Fall 2026 and 12 units. Its linked syllabus.html is a lecture/chapter schedule without its own course identifier or year; it was reviewed but not promoted as an independently identified full syllabus. Catalog prerequisites remain authoritative metadata.

2026-10-11 independent core subject review: 15-213 is systems, not foundations merely because it appears in the Computer Science core table. Nine fixed records now comprise4foundations,1systems,2AI/ML and2explicitly unclassified seminar/orientation records. All broader elective/degree-wide subject classifications remain a separate ongoing correctness audit; requirement inventory completeness is not taxonomy certification.
